_notes: THE CONTACT BURST, ALONE. fire_contact_8f.png is 1774x887 over 4x2, same
non-dividing sheet shape as water's and the same README-stated boundaries
rects, the README's own numbers, for the same reason water's notes give:
a floor-divided grid drifts two pixels short of the true cell by the fourth
column.
MEASURED: unlike water's contact sheet (5 of 8 cells touching a cell edge)
and unlike wind's and earth's below, NONE of fire's eight cells touch an edge
at alpha threshold 8. The flame burst stays inside its own cell at every stage,
so explicit rects here are the README's convention rather than a clipping
correction -- stated for consistency and because the boundaries genuinely are
444/443 alternating, not because a defect was found.
THE SEQUENCE, cell by cell: c0 is a forward-pointing flame identical in
silhouette to the core's own projectile -- the APPROACHING pose, same role as
water's contact_f0 and the reason the played layer starts at startFrame 2.
c1 is a compact spike just beginning to flare. c2 opens into a six-petalled
burst. c3 is the WIDEST frame in the sheet -- 26.2% ink coverage, the
runner-up (c2) is 13.8% -- a full flower of flame petals radiating outward,
same peak position (source frame 4, one-indexed) every README in this pack
names. c4-c7 break the petals apart into separate embers and thin them out;
c7 is functionally empty (0.0% ink), just a couple of drifting sparks.
CANVAS 512, same headroom reasoning as water's notes: the scale step below
grows c3 about its own centre inside the 444x444 cell and feathers the ring,
and the split-per-layer recipe's own largest cell is 444, so the padding has
to be stated rather than inferred.
contact_f0 IS NOT SCALE-CORRECTED. Water's 1.10 on its own frame 0 was a
measured bridge between two separate sheets sharing ONE combined sequence
(D21 in docs/PLAN_SPELL_LAYERS.md); the layered presentation never plays that
join because core and splash are separate layers with separate boxes, and this
recipe never played a combined sequence to begin with. Nothing to correct.
contact_f3 GETS hold: 2 AND A MODEST GROWTH (1.06), same trick as water and
safe here because f3 has headroom to spare -- it is the one frame with no
edge touch, so growing it about its own centre does not clip anything that
was not already clipped.
